doc.title: FAQs
doc.summary: This document addresses frequently asked questions about the Digii Infrastructure Management Module, covering topics such as its purpose, restrictions on deleting or editing records, the process for archiving and reactivating facilities, bulk update capabilities, and how listing filters work.

chunks.what_it_does: The Infrastructure Management Module allows institutions to create, manage, and categorize all physical infrastructures such as classrooms, labs, auditoriums, hostels, and other facilities.
chunks.why_it_matters: It helps maintain centralized data for capacity planning, bookings, and utilization tracking across various modules like Timetable, Venue Booking, Examination Management System (EMS) for seating plan and Asset Management.
examples: Tracking lab utilization for resource allocation.

chunks.what_it_does: The system does not allow deletion of infrastructure records once created, instead providing an 'Archive' feature to hide them from active lists.
chunks.why_it_matters: This restriction maintains data integrity and audit history, preventing broken references in related modules like venue bookings, assets, or timetable scheduling. Archiving ensures historical data remains accessible for reporting and compliance.
examples: An old classroom linked to past timetables cannot be deleted.
A lab that is no longer in use can be archived instead of deleted.

chunks.what_it_does: The system locks editing for 'Infrastructure Type', 'Belongs To', and 'Floor' details once an infrastructure is in use (linked to modules, bookings, or assets).
chunks.why_it_matters: This restriction prevents data inconsistency, ensuring that changes to structural attributes do not result in mismatched records across modules like active timetables or event bookings.
how_to_use: To update these details, ensure that the infrastructure has no active or upcoming bookings.
Also, ensure that no assets are currently assigned to it.
After clearing these dependencies, the fields will become editable again.
examples: Changing a classroom's building while it's part of an active timetable is prevented.
You cannot change a lab's floor if equipment is still assigned to it.

chunks.what_it_does: Archiving allows users to hide infrastructures that are no longer in active use from active lists, while retaining their historical data for reference.
chunks.why_it_matters: This is the recommended method for managing inactive facilities, ensuring data transparency and traceability without permanently deleting records or causing data inconsistencies.
how_to_use: 1. Navigate to the Infrastructure Management Module.
2. Search the specific infrastructure record you wish to archive.
3. Click on the ellipsis (three horizontal dots to open the action menu) of desired infrastructure.
4. Select "Archive" and confirm the action when prompted.
examples: Archiving a lab that is temporarily closed for renovation.
Archiving an old hostel block that is no longer used for student accommodation.

chunks.what_it_does: These filters control the display of infrastructures on the listing screen, allowing users to view either all infrastructures (active and archived) or only active ones.
chunks.why_it_matters: Effective use of these filters helps administrators maintain better control over infrastructure visibility, preventing confusion during operational tasks and enabling comprehensive review of all created facilities.
how_to_use: Use 'Show All Infrastructures' to display both active and archived infrastructures together for a complete list.
Use 'Hide Archived Infrastructures' to display only active infrastructures available for operational use (bookings, asset allocations, scheduling).
examples: An administrator uses 'Show All Infrastructures' to review all facilities ever created.
A booking manager uses 'Hide Archived Infrastructures' to see only available venues for new bookings.

chunks.what_it_does: The system provides a Bulk Update feature allowing administrators to update multiple infrastructure records simultaneously using a predefined Excel template.
chunks.why_it_matters: This feature simplifies large-scale data management, enabling efficient updates of information like names, capacities, descriptions, and disclaimers across numerous facilities.
how_to_use: 2. Fill in updated information (such as names, capacities, description, disclaimer etc.) in the template.
3. Upload the filled Excel file back into the system.
The platform will automatically process the file and update matching infrastructure records accordingly.
examples: Updating the capacity for 50 classrooms at once.
Adding a new disclaimer to all lab facilities.

chunks.what_it_does: The system allows administrators to unarchive (reactivate) infrastructures, making them available for reuse in operations like bookings, asset assignments, or timetables.
chunks.why_it_matters: This feature is useful for bringing previously inactive facilities back into academic use, ensuring flexibility in campus management and efficient resource allocation.
how_to_use: 1. Apply the "Show Archived Infrastructures" filter on the listing page.
2. Click on the ellipsis (three horizontal dots to open the action menu) of desired infrastructure.
examples: Reactivating a lab that was previously closed for maintenance.
Bringing an old building back into use for new academic programs.

chunks.what_it_does: Check-in/check-out timings defined for a particular venue can be modified, but these changes will only apply to future bookings.
chunks.why_it_matters: This ensures that existing bookings are not disrupted by changes to venue timings, maintaining consistency for already scheduled events while allowing flexibility for future planning.
examples: If a venue's check-out time is changed from 5 PM to 6 PM, all bookings made after this change will reflect the new 6 PM check-out.
Existing bookings for the same venue will retain their original check-out times.
